items.title: Danish Outsider Magnus Bak Klaris Shocks WorldTour Pros to Win UCI Gravel Worlds
items.snippet: Gravel specialist Magnus Bak Klaris outsmarted and outsprinted heavyweight road pros in Nannup to claim the ultimate off-road rainbow jersey.
body: The fifth edition of the UCI Gravel World Championships delivered high drama in Nannup, Australia, where dedicated gravel specialist Magnus Bak Klaris triumphed over a star-studded group of WorldTour road pros.

After a grueling 144km course featuring nearly 3,713 meters of climbing and slippery, technical surfaces, a small lead group contested the finish. Benefiting from clever team tactics with compatriot Mads Würtz Schmidt, Bak Klaris played his cards perfectly in the finale.

When Würtz Schmidt crashed on a slick downhill corner with three kilometers to go, it momentarily disrupted the lead group. Bak Klaris used the chaos to bide his time, ultimately surfing Connor Swift's early sprint to secure the biggest victory of his career.
more: The race was a relentless wearing-down process. An early breakaway consisting of Lukas Pöstlberger, Jenson Young, Peter Schulting, and Jo Pirotte established an advantage of over two and a half minutes before the intense climbing and sustained chasing behind reeled them back in.

As the distance took its toll, the front group fractured. Inside the final 10 kilometers, ten riders remained together until Würtz Schmidt surged on an uphill section. Swift and Bak Klaris immediately bridged the gap, while defending champion Florian Vermeersch—who won in 2024 and finished second in previous editions—had to dig deep to claw his way back to the front.

Würtz Schmidt's late crash with just over three kilometers remaining cost him dearly, though he heroically scrambled back to the leading quartet with 1.4 kilometers left. That effort left him spent, but it paved the way for teammate Bak Klaris to take up the mantle.

In the final sprint, Ineos Grenadiers rider Connor Swift launched a powerful acceleration but went far too early, fading before the line. Vermeersch found himself boxed in on the wrong side of the road, leaving Bak Klaris to time his effort to perfection and snatch the world title ahead of Vermeersch, Swift, and Würtz Schmidt, who all crossed in the exact same time.

The victory carries extra resonance given that Bak Klaris has often had to self-fund his racing efforts, making his ascension to the top step of the world podium a profoundly rewarding moment for dedicated gravel specialists fighting for recognition against deep-pocketed WorldTour squads.

items.title: Putting the Hype to the Test: Silca Protocol RCG-3 Gravel Tires
items.snippet: Silca’s long-awaited entry into gravel rubber generated massive buzz, but do these high-volume tires actually live up to the lofty claims?
body: Silca has spent years building a massive following in the gravel community through podcasts, accessories, and sponsored athletes. When the brand finally released its much-teased tire lineup over the summer, initial stock vanished almost instantly.

While testing data and rider feedback are still rolling in, early reviews suggest the knobbier RCG-3 tread pattern in a voluminous 55mm width genuinely delivers on speed and grip. Testers running low pressures on rugged terrain found that the tire successfully balances suppleness with structural integrity.

Rather than feeling squishy or vague through corners, the high-volume casing floats over small rock steps while maintaining predictable cornering traction and surprisingly fast rolling speeds on tarmac.
more: Silca’s tire lineup features distinct tread patterns, with the RCG-1 billed as the brand's outright speed option. However, for most real-world riding conditions, the RCG-3 offers a more versatile tread profile. Silca has designed its ecosystem heavily around a 55mm width, encouraging riders to adopt higher-volume setups despite frame clearance limitations on older bikes.

Initial rolling resistance data from independent testers using the Chung Method on rough gravel shows promising results. The RCG-3 adds only a minor penalty in watts compared to ultra-fast slick alternatives, yet it provides significantly more mechanical grip and vibration damping over loose, chunky terrain.

During field testing across varied desert landscapes featuring sharp rocks, loose jeep track, and post-monsoon sandy patches, riders pushed the limits by dropping pressures down to 19-21 PSI on compliant wheel setups. Even below recommended pressure windows, the sidewalls resisted diving in hard, fast-sweeping corners.

The closest direct comparison in the market is the Vittoria Peyote, sharing a similarly efficient low-profile knob layout. However, Silca's rounded profile prioritizes straight-line speed while maintaining confident cornering stability. The primary critique from testers isn't about performance, but rather availability: critics argue Silca should fully commit to the 55mm standard rather than diluting focus with narrower variants.
Ultimately, for riders willing to embrace the wide-tire movement, the RCG-3 proves that sometimes heavily hyped products can justify their steep price tags with tangible out-on-the-road performance.

items.title: Stress Testing Six Radically Different Gravel Bikes in Squamish
items.snippet: From aero speedsters to drop-bar mountain bikes, a new field test pushes extreme rigs to their absolute limits to find the future of gravel.
body: What does the future of gravel cycling look like? To find out, a tech crew took six radically different progressive gravel bikes to the rugged outdoor playground of Squamish, British Columbia.
The test fleet spans a massive design spectrum, including aero frames with massive tire clearance, progressive race geometry, and rugged drop-bar mountain bikes capable of tackling rowdy singletrack.

To isolate how the frames perform, testers mounted identical 50mm Schwalbe control tires across all six bikes, putting them through rigorous challenges focusing on climbing, descending, and rolling efficiency.
more: The testing roster brought together riders with wildly different backgrounds: former mountain biker Mike Levy, long-distance endurance engine Josh Ross, and former Unbound top-20 finisher Logan Jones-Wilkins. Their contrasting riding styles ensured every bike was judged through multiple performance lenses.

The bike lineup itself highlights how fractured and experimental the gravel market has become. Entries include the Giant Revolt Advanced SL as a benchmark all-rounder, the ultra-endurance-focused Factor Sarana, the radical aero-profiled Argon 18 Anti Matter, and the progressive racing Obed GVR.

Pushing further into the boundary-blurring category are machines like the Pivot Les SL Drop Bar and the Salsa Fargo 32 Ti, which challenge the very definition of what a drop-bar bike can handle. These rigs lean heavily into mountain bike geometry, offering massive tire clearances up to 60mm.

The testing protocol was divided into distinct trials. Logan tackled an off-road climbing test complete with rocks, roots, and brutal interval gradients. Levy took charge of the descending challenge, pushing the rigs down technical singletrack well past conventional gravel limits. Meanwhile, Josh handled the efficiency test, maintaining a steady 200 watts over washboard fire roads.

By subjecting these diverse machines to identical control components, the field test cuts through marketing hype to reveal how different frame designs handle the shifting demands of modern gravel riding.

items.title: Tobias Kongstad Sprints to Victory at Big Sugar Classic
items.snippet: After a hard day in the break and a chase back to the front, the Danish racer timed his final acceleration perfectly in Bentonville.
body: Tobias Mørch Kongstad secured a hard-fought victory at the Life Time Big Sugar Classic gravel race in Bentonville, Arkansas, leading out a nine-rider sprint to the line.

The PAS Racing rider, who also finished third at this year's grueling Unbound Gravel 200, animated the race early by joining the primary breakaway before having to fight his way back to the lead pack.
When the dust settled after 4 hours, 36 minutes, and 3 seconds of racing, Kongstad held off Life Time Grand Prix heavyweights Mārtiņš Blūms and Cole Paton to take the top step.
more: The Big Sugar Classic serves as a crucial battleground in the American gravel calendar, drawing top international talent and domestic series contenders to the punchy, rolling terrain of Northwest Arkansas.

Kongstad's ability to infiltrate the early breakaway demonstrated his tactical aggression, but the true test came after the race regrouped. Managing energy reserves on the punchy climbs and technical descents of the Ozarks is essential for anyone hoping to contest a late-race sprint.

Entering the final kilometers with a select group of nine riders, positioning was everything. Rather than getting swamped by the powerful Grand Prix contenders massed at the front, Kongstad opened his sprint early enough to catch his rivals off guard.
Mārtiņš Blūms crossed in second place for Velo Express, while Giant-RCC's Cole Paton rounded out the podium in third, securing valuable series points.

The win cements Kongstad's status as a formidable force on the international gravel scene, proving that his early-season podium at Unbound was no fluke and showcasing his ability to read tactical gravel races to perfection.

items.title: Eneco Tour Rapidly Equalizes Prize Money After Public Call-Out
items.snippet: Organizers closed a massive pay gap between men's and women's races in the Netherlands following a viral social media critique.
body: Organizers of the concurrent men's and women's Eneco Tour events in the Netherlands moved swiftly to equalize prize money following public criticism from Dutch sprinter Charlotte Kool.
After four days of racing, Kool took to Instagram to highlight the stark financial disparity, pointing out that the women's total prize pool stood at €17,205 compared to €63,465 for the men.
Prompted by the high-profile call-out, promoters TIG Sports & Events eliminated the €46,215 pay gap entirely, bringing parity to both fields.
more: The swift institutional response highlights the growing influence of riders utilizing direct public communication channels to demand fair treatment within professional cycling.

Disparities in prize money, broadcast production, and race support have long been a flashpoint in the sport. While major classics and world championships have increasingly moved toward equal payouts, many multi-day regional stage races have lagged behind in structural equity.

Charlotte Kool, a prominent sprinter in the women's peloton, leveraged her platform to force an immediate accounting from race stakeholders. Rather than waiting for a delayed review at the end of the season, the organizers acted mid-race.

The decision sets a vital precedent for other tier-two and tier-three events across the European cycling calendar, proving that public accountability can yield immediate corrections to systemic imbalances in professional sports funding.

items.title: Road-Oriented Build Plan for a Steel Nordest Albarda Gravel Frame
items.snippet: A Reddit rider shares a meticulous plan to transform a rugged steel gravel frame into a sleek, road-leaning machine.
body: Building up a custom bike involves navigating a maze of compatibility questions, headtube standards, and component tiers. One cyclist on r/gravelcycling mapped out a road-oriented build plan around a steel Nordest Albarda frame.
Community members weighed in with practical advice on everything from carbon fork swaps and external headset solutions to wheelset weight savings.

While upgrading to a lightweight carbon fork can dramatically drop front-end weight, commenters cautioned against rushing into unproven electronic groupsets when mechanical setups offer field-serviceable reliability.
more: The core discussion centered on optimizing the balance between road speed and gravel versatility. The original steel frame offers classic aesthetics and compliance, but its stock fork is relatively heavy at over a kilogram. Swapping to a lightweight carbon aftermarket fork can shave roughly 650 grams off the front end.

However, doing so requires careful geometry calculations. Adding an external bottom headset to accommodate a modern tapered steerer tube alters the axle-to-crown height and can slightly slacken the steering angle, pushing the handling characteristics further away from a traditional road feel.

On the drivetrain front, community veterans advised prioritizing wheel upgrades before experimenting with niche electronic shifting. Shedding rotational weight from the wheelset yields an immediate, noticeable improvement in acceleration and climbing efficiency.

For budget-conscious builders, sticking with mechanical shifting ensures that roadside mechanicals remain straightforward to fix without needing proprietary diagnostic tools or batteries, keeping the adventure rolling smoothly even when far from a bike shop.

items.title: Celebrating a Major Milestone: A Rider's First 20-Mile Mixed-Surface Loop
items.snippet: From completely sedentary to riding three times a week, a beginner cyclist shares the joy of hitting a personal distance milestone.
body: For experienced cyclists accustomed to massive century rides, a 20-mile spin might seem modest. But for a community member sharing their journey on Reddit, it represented a monumental personal milestone.

Starting the year completely inactive and dealing with health struggles, the rider committed to making a change, losing significant weight and building a consistent routine of riding at least three times a week.
A Friday evening loop connecting four local parks—alternating between paved paths and crushed gravel—provided the perfect backdrop to celebrate the turnaround with a few scenic photo stops.
more: The psychological and physical hurdles of starting from zero fitness can feel insurmountable. Finding an accessible local route that mixes smooth pavement with forgiving gravel surfaces offers an ideal entry point for building both aerobic endurance and bike handling confidence.
Mixed-surface park connectors allow riders to ease into cycling without contending with aggressive vehicular traffic, making it easier to focus on cadence, hydration, and mechanical familiarity.

Stories like this highlight the quiet, transformative power of cycling as a personal outlet. Whether someone is chasing a UCI world championship rainbow jersey or simply rediscovering their physical health on a local multi-use path, the fundamental joy of two wheels remains entirely universal.

items.title: Fem van Empel Returns to Racing After Nearly a Year Away
items.snippet: The three-time cyclo-cross world champion made her long-awaited return to competition at the Berencross in Meulebeke.
body: Nearly fifty weeks after pinning on her last race number and stepping away for an extended mental and physical break, three-time cyclo-cross world champion Fem van Empel has returned to competitive action.
Making her comeback at the C2 Berencross in Meulebeke, Belgium, she debuted a fresh setup with Specialized TMRW and a renewed mindset.
Despite her lengthy absence from the peloton, she narrowly missed the podium, finishing a respectable fourth place and expressing immense gratitude for the journey back to the start line.
more: Taking a step back at the peak of dominance is a daunting choice for professional athletes, but burnout in elite cycling is an increasingly recognized hurdle. Van Empel's extended hiatus allowed her to reset away from the relentless pressure cooker of the WorldCup calendar.

Returning to high-intensity racing after nearly a year away requires immense patience. The speed, technical precision, and anaerobic demands of cyclo-cross are notoriously unforgiving, making a near-podium finish on day one a strong indicator of her underlying class and preparation.

As she reintegrates into the racing calendar with her new equipment setup, her presence instantly elevates the competitiveness of the women's field, setting up an exciting winter of mud, barriers, and tactical racing.
